tasks.q: Why does a larger cache usually improve performance?
a: More instructions and data can be kept close to the CPU, so it waits for RAM less often
It makes the hard drive faster
tasks.fb: Fetching from cache is much quicker than fetching from RAM.

tasks.q: Which level of cache is the fastest?
tasks.fb: L1 is closest to the core, so it's the quickest but also the smallest.

tasks.q: Why might a quad-core CPU not be four times faster?

Cores can only run one at a time
Extra cores slow down the clock
tasks.fb: Some jobs have to be done step by step, so extra cores sit waiting.

tasks.q: What is meant by a single core 2.5 GHz processor?
a: It has one processing unit that carries out 2.5 billion cycles per second
tasks.fb: This is a real exam question worth 2 marks: one for each part.

tasks.q: Which change would most help a CPU run several programs at the same time?
tasks.fb: Each core can work on a different task.

info.title: Turbo boost
info.text: Many CPUs speed themselves up automatically for short bursts when there's lots of work, then slow down again to stay cool.

info.title: World records
info.text: Enthusiasts have overclocked CPUs past 9 GHz using liquid nitrogen to keep them cold, but only for a few minutes.

info.title: Cache sizes
info.text: Cache is measured in megabytes, while RAM is measured in gigabytes. Cache is tiny, but much faster.

info.title: Phones have many cores
info.text: Many smartphones have eight cores: some powerful ones for games and some low-power ones to save battery.

info.title: It's not just the CPU
info.text: The amount of RAM, the speed of storage and the graphics card also affect how fast a computer feels.

info.title: Hertz
info.text: The unit hertz is named after Heinrich Hertz, a German physicist who proved radio waves exist.
